# Third-party notices

<!-- Generated by tools/generate-sbom.py from THIRD-PARTY-INVENTORY.json and tools/third-party-notices.template.md. Edit those files, not this one. -->

AI Footprint Tracker's original code is licensed under the MIT License. Dependencies and data keep their own licences and notices. The tables below are generated from `THIRD-PARTY-INVENTORY.json`, which records the exact installed versions and declared licence expressions; `SBOM.cdx.json` lists the same components and data in CycloneDX format. Data whose licence could not be verified says so.

## Browser extension

Each browser package ships the full upstream licence and notice files of these components under `licenses/`, listed in `licenses/inventory.json` and linked from `licenses.html`. WXT and Vite are build tools, but each places small runtime helpers in the extension's code, so their notices ship too.

{{BROWSER_COMPONENTS}}

Tokenizer vocabulary assets are redistributed only with the notices in `packages/tokenizers/LICENSES/`. A tokenizer mapping is a reproducibility dependency, not evidence that a consumer website exposed complete usage.

Local file extraction uses Mozilla PDF.js, fflate, saxes and xmlchars, with core-js code bundled by PDF.js. Their notices, including the PDF.js notices for its bundled fonts, colour profiles and image decoders, are preserved in each browser package. These parsers run locally; their inclusion does not imply provider OCR, rendered document visibility or complete request usage coverage.

## Website

The website build lists the components it ships, with their full licence texts, on its open-source page. The build fails if it bundles a package that the list does not include.

## Server

These Python packages run in the organization server. Container base images and deployment software such as PostgreSQL and Nginx remain separate works with their own image and source notices.

{{SERVER_COMPONENTS}}

## EcoLogits

The estimator includes an independent TypeScript port derived from EcoLogits source files. EcoLogits is developed by its contributors and is part of CodeCarbon (https://github.com/mlco2/ecologits). The derived files remain under MPL-2.0 and keep their `SPDX-License-Identifier: MPL-2.0` headers; files that adapt a specific EcoLogits module name it in a "Derived from EcoLogits" line. Project-authored wrappers do not relicense them. The corresponding source is `packages/ecologits-core` in the public repository and `source/ecologits-source.zip` in each browser package, which also carries the MPL-2.0 text, the notice and the citation file under `licenses/ecologits/`. The organization server uses the unmodified EcoLogits Python package, also under MPL-2.0.

The EcoLogits methodology documentation (https://ecologits.ai/latest/methodology/) is licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0. The project's methodology page cites and links to it; it does not copy or relicense that documentation. EcoLogits asks users to cite this article: Rincé, S. and Banse, A. (2025). EcoLogits: Evaluating the Environmental Impacts of Generative AI. Journal of Open Source Software, 10(111), 7471. https://doi.org/10.21105/joss.07471

The data sources above follow the EcoLogits methodology (https://ecologits.ai/latest/methodology/llm_inference/ and https://ecologits.ai/latest/methodology/video_generation/). Parameter counts of closed models are EcoLogits' own estimates, not vendor figures.

## Provider names

Provider names identify compatibility targets. AI Footprint Tracker is an independent project and is not affiliated with or endorsed by OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Perplexity, ML.ENERGY, EcoLogits or CodeCarbon.
